{{Family name hatnote|Gargallo|González|lang=Spanish}}{{short description|Peruvian-Chilean researcher}}
'''Ligia Gargallo González''' is a Chilean chemist and university professor of the [[Pontifical Catholic University of Chile]]. 

== Career ==
She works at the [[University of Tarapacá]] ([[Arica]]) and at the [[Pontifical Catholic University of Chile]], in [[Santiago]]. She received a bachelor's degree in chemical pharmaceutical at the [[University of Chile]] in 1959, degrees in chemistry from [[Paris Dauphine University]] and [[KU Leuven|Katholieke Universiteit Leuven]], a doctorate in chemical sciences at the [[University of Liège]] in [[Belgium]] in 1972, and a doctorate in chemistry from [[KU Leuven|Katholieke Universiteit Leuven]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://w1.conicyt.cl/bases/fondecyt/personas/4/0/4049.html|title=GARGALLO GONZALEZ, LIGIA TERESITA|website=w1.conicyt.cl|access-date=2018-03-29}}</ref> Her areas of investigation are focused in [[Polymer]]s and [[Macromolecule]]s. Her work has aided drug designers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://portal.unesco.org/science/en/ev.php-URL_ID=5212&URL_DO=DO_TOPIC&URL_SECTION=201.html|archive-url=http://webarchive.loc.gov/all/20150412060238/http://portal.unesco.org/science/en/ev.php-URL_ID=5212&URL_DO=DO_TOPIC&URL_SECTION=201.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2015-04-12|title=Five outstanding women scientists receive L'ORÉAL-UNESCO Awards for Women in Science 2007: SCIENCE|work=unesco.org}}</ref> She is the winner of the [[L'Oréal-UNESCO Awards for Women in Science|Prize L'Oréal-UNESCO to Women in Science 2007]] and Chile's [[National Prize for Natural Sciences (Chile)|National Prize for Natural Sciences]] in 2014 because of the "pioneering work in the development of the chemistry of polymers and macromolecules".
